## What does instant coffee price mean for an Indian kitchen?

Walk into any Indian kitchen and the coffee jar is usually the first thing you reach for in the morning. What you pay for it decides whether that daily ritual feels like a smart habit or a quiet compromise. A jar that costs less often stretches the definition of coffee with fillers, while a higher price can just mean better packaging rather than better beans. The sweet spot is knowing exactly what you are getting per gram. Purity Beans keeps that math transparent: the Ultra Blend at 70% coffee and 30% chicory starts at ₹209 for 50g, the agglomerated Bold pure coffee at ₹239 for 50g, and the freeze-dried Purista and Purica at ₹319 and ₹329 for 50g respectively. ## How do you read the chicory line on the jar?

Turn the jar around and find the ingredient list. That is where the truth lives. If the word chicory appears, it is there. If it does not, the jar is pure coffee. Purity Beans prints the line clearly so you never have to guess. Bold, Purista, and Purica show coffee and nothing else. Prima, our Premium Agglomerate Arabica, is also pure coffee; it is agglomerated, not freeze-dried. A quick rule of thumb: the higher the chicory percentage, the darker and heavier the cup tends to feel. Pure coffee leans brighter and more aromatic. Prices reflect the blend: Bold at ₹239 for 50g, Purista at ₹319, Purica at ₹329, and Ultra Blend at ₹209. Bigger jars drop the per-gram cost if you drink daily. Next time you stock up, scan that line first. It tells you exactly what you are paying for.

## Which jar suits the way you drink coffee?

Choosing the right Purity Beans jar comes down to how you actually drink your coffee. If you take it black and want a serious morning kick, Bold (₹239 for 50 g, ₹369 for 100 g) is agglomerated pure coffee built for that exact moment. Prefer milk? For the days you want café-quality black coffee without equipment, the freeze-dried gourmet pair makes sense: Purista Robusta (₹319 / ₹509) brings bold body and natural crema, while Purica Arabica (₹329 / ₹559) leans sweet with caramel and chocolate notes. A practical tip: grab the 50 g jars first to learn your preference, then size up to 100 g once the morning ritual is locked in.

## What does each jar cost in rupees?

The Purity Beans lineup covers a few different budgets without hiding anything. Bold, which is agglomerated pure coffee with zero chicory, sits at ₹239 for 50g and ₹369 for 100g — a solid middle ground if you want strength without filler. If you are deciding between the two gourmet granules, the 50g Gourmet Duo Mini at ₹570 lets you taste both side by side for less than buying them separately.

## How do people brew instant coffee in Indian cities?

Walk into any apartment kitchen in Bangalore or Delhi at 7 a.m. and the ritual looks surprisingly similar: a steel tumbler, a spoon that has seen thousands of stirs, and a jar of instant coffee within arm's reach. Most people just boil water in an electric kettle, drop in a heaped spoonful, add sugar if that's their thing, and pour in hot milk straight from the packet. Some swear by the 'pull' — pouring the mixture back and forth between tumbler and davara until a thin layer of foam crowns the surface. Others keep it quiet: mug, microwave, thirty seconds, done. The real difference shows up in what's inside the jar. If your morning cup tastes flat, try heating the milk just until tiny bubbles form at the edges — not a full boil — and stir the coffee into a splash of hot water first. That small pause changes everything.
